# SchemaFlux

> A compiler for structured data. Zero dependencies. Single binary.

## Pages
- [CLI Usage](https://schemaflux.dev/cli-usage.html): Reference for the schemaflux command-line interface. Build static sites from structured data with a single command.
- [Compiler Passes](https://schemaflux.dev/compiler-passes.html): SchemaFlux runs 12 ordered passes that transform the intermediate representation: slug resolution, sorting, enrichment, taxonomy grouping, related entity scoring, and more.
- [Configuration Reference](https://schemaflux.dev/configuration.html): Complete reference for the schemaflux.yaml configuration file. Covers site settings, paths, data schema, taxonomies, pagination, structured data, and output options.
- [Getting Started](https://schemaflux.dev/getting-started.html): Install SchemaFlux and build your first static site in minutes. Requires Go 1.25 or later.
- [Markdown Renderer](https://schemaflux.dev/markdown-renderer.html): SchemaFlux includes a custom markdown-to-HTML renderer built entirely with the Go standard library. No external markdown libraries are used.
- [Overview](https://schemaflux.dev/overview.html): SchemaFlux is a compiler for structured data. It reads entities with metadata, enriches them through an ordered pass pipeline, and emits output through pluggable backends.
- [Structured Data and SEO](https://schemaflux.dev/structured-data.html): SchemaFlux generates JSON-LD, Open Graph tags, sitemaps, RSS feeds, robots.txt, and llms.txt for comprehensive search engine optimization.
- [Taxonomies](https://schemaflux.dev/taxonomies.html): Taxonomies group entities by shared field values into browsable categories with automatic pagination, A-Z indices, and hub pages.
- [Template Engine](https://schemaflux.dev/template-engine.html): SchemaFlux uses Go's html/template with 60+ custom functions for rendering entity pages, homepages, taxonomy hubs, and more.
